On a hit, the target takes 1d8 cold damage, and its speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. The tentacle can attack a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. The damage increases to 2d8 at 5th level, 3d8 at 11th level, and 4d8 at 17th level.
[Active] (Bonus Action) On a hit, the target takes 1d8 cold damage, and its speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. (bonus action).
At 6th level, you gain a swimming speed of 40 feet, and you can breathe underwater.
[Passive] At 6th level, you gain a swimming speed of 40 feet, and you can breathe underwater.
At 10th level, you gain resistance to cold damage. In addition, while you are fully submerged in water, you can communicate simple ideas with any beast that has an innate swimming speed.
[Passive] At 10th level, gain resistance to cold damage. While fully submerged in water, you can communicate simple ideas with any beast that has an innate swimming speed.

At 14th level, your tentacle can defend you and your allies. When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to choose one of the creatures and reduce the damage by 1d8. If you reduce the damage to 0, you can make a melee spell attack against the attacker as part of the same reaction. On a hit, the attacker takes 1d8 + your Charisma modifier cold damage.
[Active] (Reaction) Can use your reaction to choose one of the creatures and reduce the damage by 1d8. (reaction).

At 18th level, you can call forth a manifestation of the deep. You can cast the evard's black tentacles spell, requiring no spell slot or material components. When you cast the spell in this way, the area of the spell is difficult terrain for creatures other than you. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
[Active] Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest. (action).
classes.warlock.subclasses.the-genie.des: You have made a pact with one of the genies, the mighty elemental rulers of the Inner Planes. A genie patron is a powerful being that can grant wishes and bend reality to its will.
classes.warlock.subclasses.the-genie.fea:
At 1st level, you learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Genie Spells table. Each of these spells counts as a warlock spell for you, but it doesn't count against your number of warlock spells you know.

1st: detect evil and good, protection from evil and good
3rd: create food and water, phantasmal killer
5th: creation, sending
7th: creation, summon elemental
9th: creation, wall of stone
11th: creation, wish
[Passive] Each of these spells counts as a warlock spell for you, but it doesn't count against your number of warlock spells you know.

At 1st level, your patron gifts you a magical vessel that grants you a measure of the genie's power. The vessel is a Tiny object, and you choose the object's nature: an oil lamp, an ornate urn, a gilded chalice, or some other similarly shaped Tiny object. While you are touching the vessel, you can use it as a spellcasting focus for your warlock spells. The vessel's AC equals your spell save DC. It has a number of hit points equal to your warlock level + your proficiency bonus, and it is immune to poison and psychic damage.

The vessel grants you the following benefits:

Elemental Gift: You gain a flying speed of 30 feet, which works only while you are not wearing heavy armor.

Limited Wish: Once per long rest, you can cast a spell of 6th level or lower from the warlock spell list, requiring no spell slot or material components.
[Active] The vessel grants you the following benefits: Elemental Gift: You gain a flying speed of 30 feet, which works only while you are not wearing heavy armor. (action).

Starting at 6th level, the vessel grants you resistance to a damage type based on your patron's kind: fire (Dao), cold (Djinni), lightning (Efreeti), or thunder (Marid). You also gain a flying speed of 30 feet, which works only while you are not wearing heavy armor.
[Passive] Also gain a flying speed of 30 feet, which works only while you are not wearing heavy armor.

At 10th level, when you or an ally within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to whisk the damaged creature into your vessel. The creature is transported to the vessel's extradimensional space, where it is safe from harm. The creature remains there until the end of your next turn or until you use this feature again. When the creature reappears, it appears in an unoccupied space of your choice within 30 feet of you. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
[Active] (Reaction) At 10th level, when you or an ally within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to whisk the damaged creature into your vessel. (reaction).

At 14th level, you can tap into the power of your genie patron to cast powerful spells. Once per long rest, you can cast a spell of 6th level or lower from the warlock spell list, requiring no spell slot or material components.
[Passive] At 14th level, you can tap into the power of your genie patron to cast powerful spells.
classes.warlock.subclasses.the-undead.de: You've made a pact with a powerful undead being, such as a vampire, lich, or mummy lord. This patron grants you power over death and undeath, allowing you to channel the chill of the grave and command the spirits of the dead.
classes.warlock.subclasses.the-undead.fe: You can use a bonus action to transform into a terrifying visage of death. For 1 minute, you gain the following benefits: You gain temporary hit points equal to 1d10 + your warlock level. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack, you can force the target to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target is frightened of you until the end of your next turn. You can transform a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
[Active] (Bonus Action) Gain the following benefits: You gain temporary hit points equal to 1d10 + your warlock level. (bonus action).

Your patron's power changes your body. You don't need to eat, drink, or breathe. In addition, once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack, you can change the damage type of the attack to necrotic damage. While you are in your Form of Dread, you can also change the damage type of any spell you cast to necrotic damage.
[Passive] In addition, once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack, you can change the damage type of the attack to necrotic damage.

Your body is suffused with necrotic energy. You have resistance to necrotic damage. In addition, when you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can drop to 1 hit point instead, and each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you takes necrotic damage equal to your warlock level + your Charisma modifier. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
[Active] In addition, when you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can drop to 1 hit point instead, and each creature of your choice within 30.

As an action, you can project your spirit from your body. Your body is unconscious and appears dead while your spirit is projected. Your spirit resembles a spectral version of your body and has the following statistics: It has 1 hit point and immunity to all damage except force damage. It can't take actions or cast spells. It can move through creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It has a flying speed of 40 feet and can hover. While projected, you can use your action to return to your body. Your body regains consciousness when your spirit returns to it. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
[Active] (Action) It has a flying speed of 40 feet and can hover. (action).
classes.warlock.subclasses.undying.descr:
Your patron is a powerful undead being, such as a lich, vampire, or mummy lord. These beings have cheated death and gained immortality through dark magic, and they share some of their power with their warlock servants.

The Undying patron represents those who have transcended death, and its warlocks gain abilities that reflect this connection to undeath. They can resist disease, recover from wounds, and even cheat death itself.
classes.warlock.subclasses.undying.featu: At 1st level, you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened.
[Passive] At 1st level, you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened.
At 14th level, you can't be killed by a single attack.
[Passive] At 14th level, you can't be killed by a single attack.
At 6th level, you can gain temporary hit points when you finish a short rest.
[Passive] At 6th level, you can gain temporary hit points when you finish a short rest.
At 10th level, you can regain hit points when you take damage.
[Passive] At 10th level, you can regain hit points when you take damage.
classes.wizard.flavorText:
Wizards cast spells of explosive fire, arcing lightning, subtle deception, and spectacular transformations. A scholarly spellcaster who wields magic through study and arcane knowledge. Wizards are supreme magic-users, defined and united as a class by the spells they cast.

Wizards are supreme magic-users, defined and united as a class by the spells they cast. Drawing on the subtle weave of magic that permeates the cosmos, wizards cast spells of explosive fire, arcing lightning, subtle deception, and brute-force mind control. Their magic conjures monsters from other planes of existence, glimpses the future, or turns slain foes into zombies.

Wizards live and breathe magic. They learn it, they shape it, they call it from beyond the boundaries of the mundane world. The wizard is a scholar of the arcane, a spellcaster who wields magic through study and arcane knowledge.
classes.wizard.description:
As a student of arcane magic, you have a spellbook containing spells that show the first glimmerings of your true power. 
 
#### Cantrips 
 
At 1st level, you know three cantrips of your choice from the wizard spell list. You learn additional wizard cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Wizard table. 
 
#### Spellbook 
 
At 1st level, you have a spellbook containing six 1st- level wizard spells of your choice. Your spellbook is the repository of the wizard spells you know, except your cantrips, which are fixed in your mind.
 
> ### Your Spellbook 
> 
> The spells that you add to your spellbook as you gain levels reflect the arcane research you conduct on your own, as well as intellectual breakthroughs you have had about the nature of the multiverse. You might find other spells during your adventures. You could discover a spell recorded on a scroll in an evil wizard's chest, for example, or in a dusty tome in an ancient library. 
> 
> **_Copying a Spell into the Book._** When you find a wizard spell of 1st level or higher, you can add it to your spellbook if it is of a spell level you can prepare and if you can spare the time to decipher and copy it. 
> 
> Copying that spell into your spellbook involves reproducing the basic form of the spell, then deciphering the unique system of notation used by the wizard who wrote it. You must practice the spell until you understand the sounds or gestures required, then transcribe it into your spellbook using your own notation. 
> 
> For each level of the spell, the process takes 2 hours and costs 50 gp. The cost represents material components you expend as you experiment with the spell to master it, as well as the fine inks you need to record it. Once you have spent this time and money, you can prepare the spell just like your other spells. 
> 
> **_Replacing the Book._** You can copy a spell from your own spellbook into another book-for example, if you want to make a backup copy of your spellbook. This is just like copying a new spell into your spellbook, but faster and easier, since you understand your own notation and already know how to cast the spell. You need spend only 1 hour and 10 gp for each level of the copied spell. 
> 
> If you lose your spellbook, you can use the same procedure to transcribe the spells that you have prepared into a new spellbook. Filling out the remainder of your spellbook requires you to find new spells to do so, as normal. For this reason, many wizards keep backup spellbooks in a safe place. 
> 
> **_The Book's Appearance._** Your spellbook is a unique compilation of spells, with its own decorative flourishes and margin notes. It might be a plain, functional leather volume that you received as a gift from your master, a finely bound gilt-edged tome you found in an ancient library, or even a loose collection of notes scrounged together after you lost your previous spellbook in a mishap.
 
#### Preparing and Casting Spells 
 
The Wizard table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest. 
 
You prepare the list of wizard spells that are available for you to cast. To do so, choose a number of wizard spells from your spellbook equal to your Intelligence modifier + your wizard level (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. 
 
For example, if you're a 3rd-level wizard, you have four 1st-level and two 2nd-level spell slots. With an Intelligence of 16, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of 1st or 2nd level, in any combination, chosen from your spellbook. If you prepare the 1st-level spell *magic missile,* you can cast it using a 1st-level or a 2nd-level slot. Casting the spell doesn't remove it from your list of prepared spells. 
 
You can change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list of wizard spells requires time spent studying your spellbook and memorizing the incantations and gestures you must make to cast the spell: at least 1 minute per spell level for each spell on your list. 
 
#### Spellcasting Ability 
 
Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your wizard spells, since you learn your spells through dedicated study and memorization. You use your Intelligence whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Intelligence modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a wizard spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one. 
 
**Spell save DC** = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier 
 
**Spell attack modifier** = your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier 
 
#### Ritual Casting 
 
You can cast a wizard spell as a ritual if that spell has the ritual tag and you have the spell in your spellbook. You don't need to have the spell prepared. 
 
#### Spellcasting Focus 
 
You can use an arcane focus as a spellcasting focus for your wizard spells. 
 
#### Learning Spells of 1st Level and Higher 
 
Each time you gain a wizard level, you can add two wizard spells of your choice to your spellbook for free. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots, as shown on the Wizard table. On your adventures, you might find other spells that you can add to your spellbook (see the “Your Spellbook” sidebar).
 

 
You have learned to regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. Once per day when you finish a short rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your wizard level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher. 
 
For example, if you're a 4th-level wizard, you can recover up to two levels worth of spell slots. You can recover either a 2nd-level spell slot or two 1st-level spell slots. 
 

 
When you reach 2nd level, you choose an arcane tradition, shaping your practice of magic through one of eight schools: Abjuration, Conjuration, Divination, Enchantment, Evocation, Illusion, Necromancy, or Transmutation, all detailed at the end of the class description. 
 
Your choice grants you features at 2nd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level. 
 

 
When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. 
 

 
At 18th level, you have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will. Choose a 1st-level wizard spell and a 2nd-level wizard spell that are in your spellbook. You can cast those spells at their lowest level without expending a spell slot when you have them prepared. If you want to cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal. 
 
By spending 8 hours in study, you can exchange one or both of the spells you chose for different spells of the same levels. 
 

 
When you reach 20th level, you gain mastery over two powerful spells and can cast them with little effort. Choose two 3rd-level wizard spells in your spellbook as your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, they don't count against the number of spells you have prepared, and you can cast each of them once at 3rd level without expending a spell slot. When you do so, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest. 
 
If you want to cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal. 
 

 
The study of wizardry is ancient, stretching back to the earliest mortal discoveries of magic. It is firmly established in fantasy gaming worlds, with various traditions dedicated to its complex study. 
 
The most common arcane traditions in the multiverse revolve around the schools of magic. Wizards through the ages have cataloged thousands of spells, grouping them into eight categories called schools. In some places, these traditions are literally schools; a wizard might study at the School of Illusion while another studies across town at the School of Enchantment. In other institutions, the schools are more like academic departments, with rival faculties competing for students and funding. Even wizards who train apprentices in the solitude of their own towers use the division of magic into schools as a learning device, since the spells of each school require mastery of different techniques.
classes.wizard.features.spellcasting-wiz: As a student of arcane magic, you have a spellbook containing spells that show the first glimmerings of your true power.
[Passive] As a student of arcane magic, you have a spellbook containing spells that show the first glimmerings of your true power.
You have learned to regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. Once per day when you finish a short rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your wizard level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher.

For example, if you're a 4th-level wizard, you can recover up to two levels worth of spell slots. You can recover either a 2nd-level spell slot or two 1st-level spell slots.
[Active] (Special) (1 per Long Rest) You have learned to regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook.
classes.wizard.subclasses.abjuration.des:
The abjuration specialist is a wizard who focuses on protective and defensive magic. They are masters of wards, shields, and counterspells, able to protect themselves and their allies from magical and physical harm.

Abjurers study the theory and practice of defensive magic, learning to create magical barriers that can absorb damage and deflect attacks. They are often found on the front lines, using their abilities to keep their companions safe.
classes.wizard.subclasses.abjuration.fea: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy an abjuration spell into your spellbook is halved.
[Active] At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy an abjuration spell into your spellbook is halved. (action).
Also at 2nd level, you can create a magical ward.

[Passive] At 2nd level, when you cast an abjuration spell, you create a magical ward with Hit Points equal to twice your wizard level + your Intelligence modifier. The ward takes damage first and recharges when you cast an abjuration spell.
At 6th level, you can use your Arcane Ward to protect others.
[Active] At 6th level, you can use your Arcane Ward to protect others. (action).
At 10th level, your Arcane Ward regains hit points when you finish a short rest.
[Passive] At 10th level, your Arcane Ward regains hit points when you finish a short rest.
At 14th level, you have advantage on saving throws against spells.
[Passive] At 14th level, you have advantage on saving throws against spells.
classes.wizard.subclasses.bladesinging.d: Bladesingers are elves who have learned to combine swordplay with arcane magic. They are deadly warriors who use their magic to enhance their combat prowess.
classes.wizard.subclasses.bladesinging.f: When you choose this tradition at 2nd level, you gain proficiency with light armor, a one-handed melee weapon of your choice, and the Performance skill if you don't already have it.
[Active] Gain proficiency with light armor, a one-handed melee weapon of your choice, and the Performance skill if you don't already have it. (action).

Starting at 2nd level, you learn to blend your magic with your weapon work. You gain proficiency with one of the following skills of your choice: Acrobatics, Athletics, History, or Performance. You also gain proficiency with one musical instrument of your choice.
[Passive] Also gain proficiency with one musical instrument of your choice.

Starting at 2nd level, you can invoke a secret elven magic called the Bladesong, provided you aren't wearing medium or heavy armor or using a shield. It graces you with supernatural speed, agility, and focus. You can use a bonus action to start the Bladesong, which lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you are incapacitated, if you don medium or heavy armor or a shield, or if you use two hands to make an attack with a weapon. You can also dismiss the Bladesong at any time you choose (no action required). While your Bladesong is active, you gain the following benefits:

You gain a bonus to your AC equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).

Your walking speed increases by 10 feet.

You have advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks.

You gain a bonus to any Constitution saving throw you make to maintain your concentration on a spell. The bonus equals your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
[Active] (Bonus Action) Your walking speed increases by 10 feet. (bonus action).
Starting at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. Moreover, you can cast one of your cantrips in place of one of those attacks.
[Passive] Starting at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. (only when taking the attack action, permanent, scales).

At 10th level, you can direct your magic to absorb damage while your Bladesong is active. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to expend one spell slot and reduce that damage to you by an amount equal to five times the spell slot's level.
[Active] (Reaction) At 10th level, you can direct your magic to absorb damage while your Bladesong is active. (reaction).
At 14th level, you add your Intelligence modifier to the damage of your melee weapon attacks while your Bladesong is active.
[Passive] At 14th level, you add your Intelligence modifier to the damage of your melee weapon attacks while your Bladesong is active.
classes.wizard.subclasses.chronurgy-magi: Chronurgy is the study of time magic. Chronurgists learn to manipulate the flow of time, slowing it down, speeding it up, or even reversing it.

Starting at 2nd level, you can magically exert limited control over the flow of time around a creature. When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can use your reaction to roll a d8 and apply it to the roll. You can choose to use this feature after the roll, but before the DM determines whether the attack roll, ability check, or saving throw succeeds or fails. The d8 roll is added to the total if the roll is for an attack roll or ability check, or subtracted from the total if the roll is for a saving throw. You can use this feature twice, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
[Active] (Reaction) An ability check, or a saving throw, you can use your reaction to roll a d8 and apply it to the roll. (reaction).
Starting at 2nd level, you gain a bonus to your initiative rolls equal to your Intelligence modifier. In addition, you can't be surprised while you are conscious.
[Active] Starting at 2nd level, you gain a bonus to your initiative rolls equal to your Intelligence modifier. (action).

Starting at 6th level, you can use your command over time to force a creature to slow down. As an action, you can choose a creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The creature must make an Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is restrained and incapacitated until the end of your next turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
[Active] (Action) Can choose a creature you can see within 60 feet of you. (action).

At 10th level, you can store a spell in a tiny, bead-like object. As an action, you can cast a spell of 4th level or lower into the bead, which holds the spell until it is used. The bead is a Tiny object, and it has AC 10, 1 hit point, and immunity to all damage except force damage. The bead is destroyed when the spell is cast or when you die. You can have only one bead at a time, and you can't create another until the spell in the bead is cast. The bead can be used by anyone who holds it. To use the spell, the creature holding the bead must use its action to cast the spell, using your spell save DC and spell attack bonus.
[Active] (Action) The bead is a Tiny object, and it has AC 10, 1 hit point, and immunity to all damage except force damage. (action).

Starting at 14th level, you can peer into the future and see the outcome of a course of action. When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can use your reaction to ignore the roll. Instead, you can choose the result of the roll to be the highest or lowest possible. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
[Active] (Reaction) An ability check, or a saving throw, you can use your reaction to ignore the roll. (reaction).
classes.wizard.subclasses.conjuration.de:
Conjurers specialize in creating objects and creatures from nothing. They can summon weapons, armor, and even living creatures to aid them in battle or perform tasks.

The study of conjuration requires precision and spatial awareness. Conjurers learn to open portals to other planes, calling forth creatures and objects to serve their needs. They are versatile spellcasters who can adapt to any situation.
classes.wizard.subclasses.conjuration.fe: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy a conjuration spell into your spellbook is halved.
[Active] At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy a conjuration spell into your spellbook is halved. (action).
Also at 2nd level, you can conjure small objects.

[Passive] At 2nd level, you can conjure a nonmagical object in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of you. The object can be no larger than 3 feet on a side and weighs no more than 10 pounds. It disappears after 1 hour or if it takes any damage.
At 6th level, you can swap places with a creature.

[Passive] At 6th level, as a bonus action, you can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. If you teleport within 5 feet of a willing creature, you can swap places with that creature.
At 10th level, your concentration on conjuration spells is not broken when you take damage.
[Passive] At 10th level, your concentration on conjuration spells is not broken when you take damage.
At 14th level, your summoned creatures gain temporary hit points.
[Passive] At 14th level, your summoned creatures gain temporary hit points.
classes.wizard.subclasses.divination.des:
Diviners study the art of predicting the future. They can glimpse moments yet to come, gaining insight into the outcomes of actions and the intentions of others.

The study of divination requires keen intellect and intuition. Diviners learn to read the signs and portents that others miss, using their knowledge to guide their allies and outmaneuver their enemies.
classes.wizard.subclasses.divination.fea: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy a divination spell into your spellbook is halved.
[Active] At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy a divination spell into your spellbook is halved. (action).
Also at 2nd level, you can replace any attack roll, ability check, or saving throw.
[Active] Also at 2nd level, you can replace any attack roll, ability check, or saving throw. (action).
At 6th level, you can regain spell slots when you cast divination spells.
[Passive] At 6th level, you can regain spell slots when you cast divination spells.
At 10th level, you can gain darkvision, see invisible creatures, etc.
[Passive] At 10th level, you can gain darkvision, see invisible creatures, etc.
At 14th level, you can cast the foresight spell once per long rest.
[Passive] At 14th level, you can cast the foresight spell once per long rest.
classes.wizard.subclasses.enchantment.de:
Enchanters specialize in manipulating the minds of others. They can charm, beguile, and control creatures, turning enemies into allies and bending others to their will.

The study of enchantment requires subtlety and finesse. Enchanters learn to weave spells that influence thoughts and emotions, using their abilities to avoid conflict or gain advantage in social situations.
classes.wizard.subclasses.enchantment.fe: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy an enchantment spell into your spellbook is halved.
[Active] At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy an enchantment spell into your spellbook is halved. (action).
Also at 2nd level, you can charm a creature with a look.
[Passive] Also at 2nd level, you can charm a creature with a look.
At 6th level, you can divert attacks made against you.
[Passive] At 6th level, you can divert attacks made against you.
At 10th level, you can target two creatures with enchantment spells.
[Passive] At 10th level, you can target two creatures with enchantment spells.
At 14th level, you can modify a creature's memory.
[Passive] At 14th level, when you charm a creature, you can modify its memory of the event. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have its memory altered.
classes.wizard.subclasses.evocation.desc: You focus your study on magic that creates powerful elemental effects such as bitter cold, searing flame, rolling thunder, crackling lightning, and burning acid. Some evokers find employment in military forces, serving as artillery to blast enemy armies from afar. Others use their spectacular power to protect the weak, while some seek their own gain as bandits, adventurers, or aspiring tyrants.
classes.wizard.subclasses.evocation.feat: Beginning when you select this school at 2nd level, the gold and time you must spend to copy an evocation spell into your spellbook is halved.
[Active] Beginning when you select this school at 2nd level, the gold and time you must spend to copy an evocation spell into your spellbook is halved. (action).

Beginning at 2nd level, you can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your evocation spells. When you cast an evocation spell that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 + the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.
[Active] The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save. (action).

Starting at 6th level, your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against your cantrip, the creature takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.
[Passive] The creature takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.
Beginning at 10th level, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of any wizard evocation spell you cast.
[Active] Beginning at 10th level, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of any wizard evocation spell you cast. (action).

Starting at 14th level, you can increase the power of your simpler spells. When you cast a wizard spell of 1st through 5th level that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell.
The first time you do so, you suffer no adverse effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a long rest, you take 2d12 necrotic damage for each level of the spell, immediately after you cast it. Each time you use this feature again before finishing a long rest, the necrotic damage per spell level increases by 1d12. This damage ignores resistance and immunity.
[Active] Each time you use this feature again before finishing a long rest, the necrotic damage per spell level increases by 1d12. (action).
classes.wizard.subclasses.graviturgy-mag: Graviturgy is the study of gravity magic. Graviturgists learn to manipulate the force of gravity, making themselves and their allies lighter or heavier, and even creating gravitational anomalies.

Starting at 2nd level, you can use your command of gravity to alter the weight of a creature. As an action, you can choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The creature must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the creature's weight is halved or doubled (your choice) for 1 minute. While the creature's weight is halved, its walking speed increases by 10 feet, and it has advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. While the creature's weight is doubled, its walking speed decreases by 10 feet, and it has disadvantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
[Active] (Action) Its walking speed increases by 10 feet, and it has advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. (action).

Starting at 6th level, you can create a point of intense gravitational force. When you cast a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw, you can choose one creature that fails its saving throw. That creature is pulled 10 feet toward you, provided you can see it and it is within 60 feet of you.
[Active] That creature is pulled 10 feet toward you, provided you can see it and it is within 60 feet of you. (action).

Starting at 10th level, you can use your command of gravity to increase the force of your attacks. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can use a bonus action to choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. That creature takes force damage equal to your Intelligence modifier, and you can move it 10 feet toward you or away from you (your choice). You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
[Active] (Bonus Action) That creature takes force damage equal to your Intelligence modifier, and you can move it 10 feet toward you or away from you (your choice). (bonus action).

At 14th level, you can create a devastating gravitational anomaly. As an action, you can choose a point you can see within 120 feet of you. Each creature in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 5d10 force damage and is restrained until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't restrained. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
[Active] (Action) On a failed save, a creature takes 5d10 force damage and is restrained until the start of your next turn. (action).
classes.wizard.subclasses.illusion.descr:
Illusionists create false images and manipulate perceptions. They can make things appear or disappear, create phantasmal creatures, and alter the appearance of themselves and others.

The study of illusion requires creativity and imagination. Illusionists learn to bend light and sound, creating realistic illusions that can deceive even the most perceptive observers.
classes.wizard.subclasses.illusion.featu: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy an illusion spell into your spellbook is halved.
[Active] At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy an illusion spell into your spellbook is halved. (action).
Also at 2nd level, you can change the nature of your illusions.
[Passive] Also at 2nd level, you can change the nature of your illusions.
At 10th level, you can make an illusion real.
[Passive] At 10th level, when a creature makes an attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to create an illusory duplicate of yourself, causing the attack to miss you instead.
At 14th level, you can create an illusory creature.
[Passive] At 14th level, you can create an illusory creature.
classes.wizard.subclasses.necromancy.des:
Necromancers study the forces of life and death. They can animate the dead, drain life force from living creatures, and even cheat death itself.

The study of necromancy requires a strong will and a willingness to confront the darker aspects of existence. Necromancers learn to harness the power of negative energy, using it to create undead servants and protect themselves from harm.
classes.wizard.subclasses.necromancy.fea: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy a necromancy spell into your spellbook is halved.
[Active] At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy a necromancy spell into your spellbook is halved. (action).
Also at 2nd level, you can regain hit points when you kill a creature.
[Passive] Also at 2nd level, you can regain hit points when you kill a creature.
At 6th level, you can animate undead.
[Passive] At 6th level, when you raise a creature as an undead, it gains additional Hit Points and your proficiency bonus to its attacks and damage rolls. You can also command it as a bonus action.
At 10th level, you have resistance to necrotic damage.
[Passive] At 10th level, you have resistance to necrotic damage.
At 14th level, you can command undead creatures.

[Passive] At 14th level, you can use your action to target one undead creature within 60 feet of you. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you for 1 minute. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses on a long rest.
classes.wizard.subclasses.order-of-scrib: The Order of Scribes is a tradition of wizards who believe that magic is a language. They study the written word and the arcane symbols that make up spells, and they use their knowledge to create new spells and modify existing ones.

At 2nd level, you can use a special quill to write spells into your spellbook. The quill doesn't require ink. When you use the quill to copy a spell into your spellbook, you can reduce the time and cost to copy the spell by half. You can also use the quill to create a spell scroll. When you do so, you must provide the spell's components, and the scroll costs half the normal amount of gold to create.
[Active] Can also use the quill to create a spell scroll. (action).

Starting at 2nd level, you have a spellbook that has been awakened by your magic. The spellbook has the following benefits:

You can use the spellbook as a spellcasting focus for your wizard spells.

When you cast a wizard spell with a spell slot, you can temporarily replace its damage type with the damage type of another spell in your spellbook of the same level. This replacement lasts for the duration of the spell.

When you cast a wizard spell as a ritual, you can use the spell's normal casting time, rather than adding 10 minutes to it. Once you use this benefit, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

If your spellbook is lost, you can perform a special ritual to create a new one. This ritual takes 8 hours to complete, and you must have access to a wizard's spellbook to copy spells from. The new spellbook becomes your awakened spellbook.
[Active] This ritual takes 8 hours to complete, and you must have access to a wizard's spellbook to copy spells from. (action).

Starting at 6th level, you can cause your spellbook to manifest a spectral mind. As a bonus action, you can cause the mind to appear in an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet of you. The mind is a Tiny object, and it has AC 10, 1 hit point, and immunity to all damage except force damage. The mind is invisible, and it can't be targeted by attacks or spells. The mind lasts for 1 hour, until you dismiss it as a bonus action, or until you die. While the mind is present, you can use it as a spellcasting focus for your wizard spells. In addition, you can cast spells as if you were in the mind's space, provided you can see the mind.
[Active] (Bonus Action) Can cause the mind to appear in an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet of you. (bonus action).

Starting at 10th level, you can create powerful scrolls. When you finish a long rest, you can create a number of spell scrolls equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one). The scrolls must be for spells of 5th level or lower, and the spells must be in your spellbook. The scrolls cost half the normal amount of gold to create, and they last for 8 hours before becoming inert.
[Active] The scrolls cost half the normal amount of gold to create, and they last for 8 hours before becoming inert. (action).

At 14th level, your mastery of the written word allows you to cast spells without speaking. When you cast a wizard spell, you can cast it without verbal components. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
[Active] Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest. (action).
Transmuters manipulate the physical world. They can change the shape and properties of objects, transform one substance into another, and even alter their own bodies.

The study of transmutation requires a deep understanding of the natural world. Transmuters learn to reshape reality at a fundamental level, using their abilities to adapt to any situation and overcome any obstacle.
At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy a transmutation spell into your spellbook is halved.
[Active] At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy a transmutation spell into your spellbook is halved. (action).
Also at 2nd level, you can transmute materials.
[Passive] At 2nd level, you can transmute one object into another material of the same size and value. The effect lasts for 1 hour or until the object takes any damage.
At 6th level, you can create a stone that grants benefits.
[Passive] At 6th level, you can create a stone that grants benefits.
At 10th level, you can cast the polymorph spell on yourself.
[Passive] At 10th level, you can cast the polymorph spell on yourself.
At 14th level, you can transmute matter at a touch.
[Passive] At 14th level, you can transmute matter at a touch.
classes.wizard.subclasses.war-magic.desc: The War Magic tradition is a school of wizardry that focuses on the practical application of magic in combat. War mages are skilled in both offensive and defensive magic, and they use their knowledge to survive on the battlefield.
classes.wizard.subclasses.war-magic.feat: At 2nd level, you learn to weave your magic into a protective shield. When you are hit by an attack or you fail a saving throw against a spell or other magical effect, you can use your reaction to gain a +2 bonus to your AC against that attack or a +4 bonus to that saving throw. If you do so, you can't cast spells other than cantrips until the end of your next turn.
[Active] (Reaction) Can use your reaction to gain a +2 bonus to your AC against that attack or a +4 bonus to that saving throw. (reaction).
Starting at 2nd level, you add your Intelligence modifier to your initiative rolls.
[Active] Starting at 2nd level, you add your Intelligence modifier to your initiative rolls. (action).

Starting at 6th level, you can store magical energy inside your body to fuel your spells. You have a pool of power surges, represented by a number of d6s equal to your wizard level. When you make an attack roll or a saving throw, you can spend one power surge to add the roll of one d6 to the total. You can use this feature only once per turn. You regain all expended power surges when you finish a long rest.
[Active] Can spend one power surge to add the roll of one d6 to the total. (action).
At 10th level, the spells you cast help sustain your defenses. While you are maintaining concentration on a spell, you gain a +2 bonus to AC and to all saving throws.
[Passive] At 10th level, while you are maintaining concentration on a spell, you gain a +2 bonus to AC and to all saving throws.

At 14th level, your Arcane Deflection becomes more powerful. When you use your Arcane Deflection, you can choose up to three creatures within 10 feet of you. The bonus you gain from Arcane Deflection is granted to those creatures as well.
[Active] Can choose up to three creatures within 10 feet of you. (action).
classes.artificer.flavorText: Masters of invention, artificers use ingenuity and magic to unlock extraordinary capabilities in objects. They see magic as a complex system waiting to be decoded and then harnessed in their spells and inventions.
classes.artificer.subclasses.alchemist.d: An Alchemist is an expert in magical chemistry, combining reagents to produce mystical effects. Alchemists use their potions and elixirs to heal allies and hinder foes.
classes.artificer.subclasses.alchemist.f: You gain proficiency with alchemist's supplies. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with another type of artisan's tools of your choice.

Whenever you finish a long rest, you can produce a number of experimental elixirs equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1). You can use a bonus action to drink one of your elixirs or administer it to another creature. The elixir produces one of the following effects (your choice): Healing (regains 2d4 + Intelligence modifier hit points), Swiftness (speed increases by 10 feet for 1 hour), or Resilience (gain a +1 bonus to AC for 10 minutes).
[Active] (Bonus Action) Whenever you finish a long rest, you can produce a number of experimental elixirs equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1).
When you cast a spell using your alchemist's supplies as the spellcasting focus, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one roll of acid, fire, necrotic, or poison damage.
[Active] Can add your Intelligence modifier to one roll of acid, fire, necrotic, or poison damage. (action).

You can cast the lesser restoration spell without expending a spell slot or requiring material components. You can do so a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
[Active] Can do so a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. (action).
You gain resistance to acid and poison damage, and you have advantage on saving throws against being poisoned.
[Passive] Gain resistance to acid and poison damage, and you have advantage on saving throws against being poisoned.
classes.artificer.subclasses.armorer.des: An Armorer uses their artificer magic to empower a suit of armor, turning it into a powerful magical protection. The Armorer can transform their armor into different modes for combat or stealth.
classes.artificer.subclasses.armorer.fea: You gain proficiency with heavy armor and smith's tools.
[Passive] Gain proficiency with heavy armor and smith's tools.

Your armor becomes magical. You can don or doff your armor as an action, and it can't be removed against your will. While wearing your armor, you gain the following benefits: You have a +1 bonus to AC, you can use your Intelligence modifier instead of Strength for attack and damage rolls with weapons, and you can use your armor as a spellcasting focus.
[Active] (Action) Can don or doff your armor as an action, and it can't be removed against your will. (action).

You can customize your armor for combat or stealth. When you finish a long rest, you can change your armor model. Choose one of the following: Guardian (you have advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks, and when you take the Attack action on your turn, you can make an additional melee attack from the armor's thunder gauntlets) or Infiltrator (you have advantage on Charisma (Stealth) checks, and your armor's lightning launcher deals an extra 1d6 lightning damage).

[Active] (Action) Choose one of the following: Guardian (you have advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks, and when you take the Attack action on your turn, you can make an additional melee attack.
You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
[Passive] Can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. (only when taking the attack action, permanent, scales).
You learn 2 additional artificer infusions, and you can apply them to your armor. You can have up to 4 infusions active on your armor at a time.
[Passive] Learn 2 additional artificer infusions, and you can apply them to your armor.

Your armor's power increases. While wearing your armor, you gain the following benefits based on your armor model: Guardian (when a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to deal 1d6 thunder damage to that creature) or Infiltrator (when you hit a creature with an attack, you can deal an additional 1d6 lightning damage).
[Active] (Reaction) Gain the following benefits based on your armor model: Guardian.
classes.artificer.subclasses.artillerist: An Artillerist specializes in harnessing the power of magic to create destructive energy. They can conjure a magical cannon that unleashes powerful blasts of elemental energy.
You gain proficiency with woodcarver's tools.

You can use woodcarver's tools and 10 gp worth of raw materials to create a Small eldritch cannon in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. The cannon has AC 18 and hit points equal to five times your artificer level. You can have only one cannon at a time. As an action, you can command the cannon to move up to 15 feet. You can use a bonus action to activate the cannon, causing it to produce one of the following effects: Flamethrower (15-foot cone, 2d8 fire damage, Dexterity saving throw), Force Ballista (ranged spell attack, 2d8 force damage, push 5 feet), or Protector (10-foot radius, 1d8 + Intelligence modifier temporary hit points).
[Active] (Bonus Action) Can use woodcarver's tools and 10 gp worth of raw materials to create a Small eldritch cannon in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. (bonus action).
You can use a wand, staff, or rod as a spellcasting focus. When you cast an artificer spell through this focus, you can roll a d8 and add it to one damage roll of the spell.
[Active] Can roll a d8 and add it to one damage roll of the spell. (action).

Your cannon's damage increases by 1d8. In addition, you can detonate your cannon as an action. Each creature within 20 feet of the cannon must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 3d8 force damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
[Active] (Action) Each creature within 20 feet of the cannon must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 3d8 force damage on a failed save, or half.
You and your allies have half cover while within 10 feet of your cannon. In addition, you can have two cannons at a time, and you can activate both with the same bonus action.
[Active] (Bonus Action) And your allies have half cover while within 10 feet of your cannon. (bonus action).
classes.artificer.subclasses.battle-smit: A Battle Smith is a master of combat and magic, combining martial prowess with magical tinkering. They can create a powerful steel defender that fights alongside them.
You gain proficiency with smith's tools and heavy armor.
[Passive] Gain proficiency with smith's tools and heavy armor. (permanent).
You are proficient with martial weapons. When you attack with a magic weapon, you can use your Intelligence modifier instead of Strength or Dexterity for the attack and damage rolls.
[Active] Can use your Intelligence modifier instead of Strength or Dexterity for the attack and damage rolls. (action).

You can use smith's tools and 10 gp worth of raw materials to create a steel defender in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. The defender has AC 15 + your proficiency bonus and hit points equal to 2 + your Intelligence modifier + five times your artificer level. It is friendly to you and your companions, and it obeys your commands. In combat, the defender shares your initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours.
[Active] Can use smith's tools and 10 gp worth of raw materials to create a steel defender in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. (action).
You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
[Passive] Can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. (only when taking the attack action, permanent, scales).

When you hit a creature with a magic weapon, you can channel a burst of arcane energy into the target. The target takes an additional 2d6 force damage, and if the target is a construct, it takes an additional 2d6 force damage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
[Active] The target takes an additional 2d6 force damage, and if the target is a construct, it takes an additional 2d6 force damage. (action).

Your Arcane Jolt and steel defender become more powerful. The extra damage of Arcane Jolt increases to 4d6. In addition, when your steel defender uses its Deflect Attack feature, the attacker takes force damage equal to 1d4 + your Intelligence modifier.
[Active] In addition, when your steel defender uses its Deflect Attack feature, the attacker takes force damage equal to 1d4 + your Intelligence modifier. (action).
